title: The Dogs and the Fox
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: Some Dogs once found a lion's skin, and were worrying it with their teeth. Just then a Fox came by, and said, "You think yourselves very brave, no doubt; but if that were a live lion you'd find his claws a good deal sharper than your teeth."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Dogs find?
According to the passage, what were the Dogs doing to the skin?
options: Dragging it back to their den

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who came by while the Dogs were worrying the skin?
According to the passage, what does the Fox say the Dogs think of themselves?
According to the Fox, what would the Dogs find sharper than their teeth if the lion were alive?
As the passage uses it, what does "worrying" mean in "were worrying it with their teeth"?
Based on the passage, what point is the Fox making about the Dogs' bravery?
options: It is only easy because the lion is dead and cannot fight back
It proves the Dogs could defeat a real lion
It shows the Dogs are stronger than any fox
It is proof the Dogs deserve to keep the skin

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: It is easy to seem brave against a danger that can no longer harm you
Dogs are naturally braver than foxes
Lions are always more dangerous than they appear
Sharp teeth matter more than sharp claws

questions.prompt: According to the passage, with what body part were the Dogs worrying the skin?
According to the passage, what kind of skin did the Dogs find?
According to the Fox, what would happen if the lion were alive rather than just a skin?
options: The Dogs would find its claws a good deal sharper than their teeth
The Dogs would easily defeat it together
The Fox would fight it instead of the Dogs
The lion would flee from the Dogs

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what best describes the tone of the Fox's remark, "You think yourselves very brave, no doubt"?
options: A genuine warning of danger to come
An offer to join in the game

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Fox bring up the lion's claws at all?
options: To remind the Dogs that a real, living lion would be a very different challenge
To warn the Dogs that a claw is hidden inside the skin
To suggest the Dogs should sharpen their own teeth
To offer to trade his claws for their teeth

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: Dogs fight off a live lion while a Fox watches in admiration
Dogs tear at a dead lion's skin, and a passing Fox points out their courage would fail against a real lion
A Fox and some Dogs argue over who found the lion's skin first
A Fox challenges some Dogs to a fight and loses
